description: Florida delta checked against FLHSMV teen laws and the Official Florida Driver License Handbook speed and zero-tolerance sections.

questions.q: The highest speed limit posted in Florida is
questions.explanation: The Official Florida Driver License Handbook states the speed limit will never be higher than 70 mph. You still must obey the limit posted on the road you are on.
questions.remember: Florida tops out at 70.

questions.q: A Florida driver under 21 with a blood alcohol level of 0.02 or higher
options: Has the license suspended six months
Loses the license for five years
questions.explanation: FLHSMV states drivers under 21 at 0.02 or more have the license suspended for six months on a first offense. A second offense is one year.
questions.remember: Under 21 at 0.02: license suspended six months.

questions.q: A Florida driver under 18 who gets 6 or more points in 12 months
options: Loses the license for a year
Is limited to business driving for a year
Must retake the road test the next day
questions.explanation: The handbook states drivers under 18 with six or more points in a 12-month period are restricted to business purposes only for one year.
questions.remember: Under 18 with 6 points: business driving only.

questions.q: In Florida, 12 points within 12 months results in
questions.explanation: Florida suspends the license for 30 days at 12 points in 12 months. Longer point windows carry longer suspensions.
questions.remember: 12 points in 12 months: 30 days off the road.

questions.q: On a two-way street in Florida, when a school bus has its stop signal out you must
options: Stop only if you are behind the bus
Stop only if children step out
questions.explanation: Traffic in both directions stops on an undivided roadway. On a divided highway with an unpaved space of at least 5 feet, a raised median, or a physical barrier, oncoming traffic does not stop.
questions.remember: Two-way street, bus stopped: both directions stop.

questions.q: Florida's Move Over law requires you to
options: Move over or slow to 20 mph under
Honk and pass in the same lane
questions.explanation: If you cannot safely change lanes away from the stopped vehicle with warning lights, you must slow to 20 mph below the posted limit. Move over a lane, or slow to 20 mph under the limit if you cannot move over, for stopped emergency, law enforcement, sanitation, and utility vehicles with lights on.
questions.remember: Move over, or slow to 20 under.

questions.q: Florida requires seat belts for
options: No one in the back seat at any age
questions.explanation: The driver and front-seat passengers must buckle up, and anyone under 18 must be restrained in any seat.
questions.remember: Front seat buckles up; under 18, every seat.

questions.q: To register and drive a vehicle in Florida you must
options: Carry no insurance if the car is paid off
Show insurance only after a crash
questions.explanation: Florida requires personal injury protection and property-damage liability at the statutory minimums to register and operate a vehicle.
questions.remember: Florida car: PIP plus property damage cover.

questions.q: Car B turned right on a red light. Car A is coming through on green. What is correct?
options: Car A goes, and Car B must yield
Car B goes because it turned first
Both cars stop in the intersection
Car A must pull onto the shoulder
questions.explanation: A right turn on red is allowed only after a stop, and that driver must yield to traffic that has the green light. Car A may go straight. Car B waits.
questions.remember: Right on red waits for the green-light car.

questions.q: These pavement markings tell you that at the intersection ahead:
options: Center lane may go straight or left
Center lane may only turn right
The center lane merges into one
Center lane traffic must turn left
questions.explanation: The left lane is marked left turn ONLY. The right lane is marked right turn ONLY. The center lane shows a straight arrow and a left arrow, so those drivers may go straight or turn left.
questions.remember: Read your lane's arrows before the corner.

questions.q: After holding a Florida learner license for three months, the learner may drive with a supervisor
questions.explanation: A Florida learner may drive only in daylight for the first three months, then until 10 p.m., always with a licensed driver 21 or older in the front seat.

provenance.section: Teen licensing requirements and driving curfews

questions.remember: After three months: until 10 p.m.

questions.q: Since January 1, 2024, Florida's Move Over law also applies when you approach
options: Any disabled vehicle stopped with hazard lights flashing
Only police cars and ambulances with sirens sounding
Only tow trucks that are actively loading a vehicle
Any vehicle parked legally on a residential street
questions.explanation: The law now covers any stopped disabled vehicle showing hazard lights, flares or emergency signs. Move over a lane, or slow to 20 mph below the limit when you cannot.
questions.remember: Hazard lights on a stopped car? Move over.

questions.q: In an active Florida school zone or work zone, a driver may use a phone
options: Only to text at a red light
questions.explanation: Section 316.306 bans hand-held wireless device use in active school zones and work zones. Hands-free use is allowed.
questions.remember: School or work zone: hands-free only.

questions.q: In Florida, if you need your windshield wipers to see in rain, you must also
questions.explanation: Section 316.217 requires headlights whenever visibility is reduced, including any time wipers are needed for rain, smoke or fog. Hazard lights are not a substitute while driving.
questions.remember: Wipers on? Headlights on.

questions.q: In Florida, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Florida issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Florida car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Florida, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Florida requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 12 months.
questions.remember: Florida: hold the permit 12 months.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 322.05 Persons not to be licensed

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Florida complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Florida requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.
questions.remember: Florida: 50 hours of supervised driving.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 322.05 Persons not to be licensed

questions.q: Of a Florida teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Florida requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Florida: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 322.05 Persons not to be licensed

questions.q: In Florida, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Florida, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.
questions.remember: Florida: driving alone from 16 years.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 322.05 Persons not to be licensed

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Florida not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Florida restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Florida new drivers: off the road 11 p.m. to 6 a.m..

questions.q: In Florida, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Florida drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.
questions.remember: Florida full license: 18 years.

provenance.manual: Licensing Requirements for Teens, Graduated Driver License Laws and Driving Curfews - Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

questions.q: How many questions are on the Florida car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Florida car knowledge test has 50 questions.
questions.remember: Florida car test: 50 questions.

provenance.manual: Class E Knowledge Exam & Driving Skills Test - Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Florida car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Florida car knowledge test.
questions.remember: Florida car test: pass with 80%.

provenance.manual: Class E Knowledge Exam & Driving Skills Test - Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Florida, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Florida, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Florida, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 316.193 Driving under the influence; penalties

questions.q: In Florida, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Florida sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.
questions.remember: Florida, under 21: 0.02%.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 322.2616 Suspension of license; persons under 21 years of age; right to review

questions.q: In Florida, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Florida brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Florida, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 322.2615 Suspension of license; right to review

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Florida residential district?
questions.explanation: Florida sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.
questions.remember: Florida residential street: 30 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Florida's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Florida: only texting is banned for all drivers.
questions.remember: Florida phone law: no texting.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 316.305 Wireless communications devices; prohibition

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Florida?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Florida, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Florida left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 316.075 Traffic control signal devices

questions.q: How is Florida's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Florida seat belt enforcement is primary.
questions.remember: Florida seat belts: primary law.

provenance.manual: Buckle Up Florida, It’s the Law! - Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Florida?
questions.explanation: Florida requires a car seat or booster until 6 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Florida: car or booster seat until 6 years.

questions.q: Under Florida's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Florida can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
questions.remember: Florida suspension: 12 points in 12 months.

provenance.manual: Florida Statutes § 322.27 Authority of department to suspend or revoke license
